reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown treat the wrestler's three titles—man, angel, and God—as referring to one figure, the covenant Angel appearing in visible human form.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Wells argues the text gives three incompatible identities for Jacob's opponent—man, God, and angel—without resolving which one is meant.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: wrestled with a man there until the breaking of the day.
sides.verseText: Jacob was left alone, and wrestled with a man there until the breaking of the day.

sides.snippet: he had power over the angel, and prevailed
sides.verseText: Indeed, he had power over the angel, and prevailed; He wept, and made supplication to him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us,
